/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 10 April 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2201 (40)
Baltic Capesize Index: 3318 (83)
Baltic Panamax Index: 1855 (13)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1308 (15)
Baltic Handysize Index: 699 (5)
CAPESIZE
The market closed the week on a firmer note, with the BCI 182 5TC advancing by $750 to settle at $30,088, reflecting a steady underlying tone across both basins. C5 edged up by $0.091 to $12.020, while C3 remained largely flat, gaining a modest $0.086 to $30.20. In the Pacific, conditions were steady throughout the day, supported by the presence of two miners on C5. While activity was not overly aggressive, it was sufficient to maintain a firm floor. Offers began the day in the low $12s, with fixtures reported at $11.95, and a miner also understood to have paid in the low $12s for earlier dates (ETA 22 April). The Atlantic showed clearer signs of improvement following the uptick in activity noted yesterday, with sentiment continuing to strengthen. This was particularly evident on fronthaul business from East Coast Canada, where stronger fixtures pushed C9 up by $2,833 to $56,889. C3 fixtures reported yesterday at $30.15 helped underpin sentiment in the basin.

Atlantic
Mercuria is reported to have fixed Highland (174,000 2006) for 170,000/10 Tubarao option West Africa to China 6/10 May at $30.15. Oldendorff was also reported to have fixed a TBN, linked to Maramaras for for 170,000/10 Tubarao option West Africa to China eta 9 May at $30.15, lacking further details.

Pacific
Rio Tinto fixed a TBN for 170,000/10 from Dampier to Qingdao 26/28 April at $11.95. FMG is reported to have fixed a Berge Bulk Newcastlemax for 190,000/10 from Port Hedland to Qingdao 22/23 April at $12.25.
PANAMAX
The market extended its positive momentum into today, with the BPI time charter average rising by $114 to close at $16.696. Rates in the Atlantic continued to firm gradually, supported by steady activity on both Trans-Atlantic and fronthaul routes. In Asia, fundamentals remained supportive, with tight prompt tonnage and a consistent flow of cargoes from NoPac and Australia sustaining demand.

Atlantic
The Eco Colonel (82,122 2012) was reported fixed for a trip from EC South America to the Red Sea at $20,500 plus a $1,000,000 ballast bonus with Damico, although some sources suggested the fixture may have failed. Additionally, the Andermatt (77,113 2015) was fixed for a similar trip from EC South America (30 April) to the Red Sea at $20,500 plus $1,050,000–$1,100,000 with Bunge, though details remain unconfirmed.

Asia
The Ever Sovereign (82,076 2017), open Rizhao 14–15 April, was heard fixed via NoPac to redelivery China at $18,350 by ASL, although further details were not disclosed.
SUPRAMAX
It was a typically slow end to the week with little in the way of fresh fixing coming to light. Sentiment remained positive for most areas and demand from the US Gulf and Asia remained in play brokers said. With the Orthodox holidays under way some preferred to wait until after the holiday be for committing. The Continent-Mediterranean again saw limited fresh enquiry and fundamentals remained unchanged. From Asia, again demand was seen as Australian business remained supported. The 11TC average closed the week up $194 from yesterday, finishing at $16,538.
HANDYSIZE
The week concluded on a relatively positive note, with rates across most loading areas trending higher compared to earlier levels. The BHSI rose by 5 points to 699 , while the 7TC average gained $79 to settle at $12,573. Across the Atlantic basin, the Continent and Mediterranean experienced some activity, though a wide bid/offer spread kept rate levels broadly unchanged. In contrast, the South Atlantic continued to show strong fundamentals, with fixtures reportedly exceeding last-done levels; a 38,000-dwt vessel was rumoured fixed from Recalada to Morocco at around $20,000, although further details remain unconfirmed. Meanwhile, the US Gulf stayed on a softer footing, as demand struggled to absorb the ample tonnage supply, maintaining downward pressure on rates. In the Pacific, despite limited reported fixtures, momentum remained firm, supported by tight tonnage availability for April dates.

Market Fundamentals
April WASDE: Wheat and Corn Stocks Raised, Soybeans Tighten on Demand

Global wheat supply for 2025/26 increased from 277.0 Mt in March to 283.1 Mt in the April WASDE, driven by higher production in the EU and Russia alongside reduced consumption, particularly in India. Global wheat exports were marginally lowered by 0.3 Mt to 221.9 Mt.

Corn stocks also edged higher, rising from 292.7 Mt to 294.8 Mt (+2.1 Mt), supported by increased output in India, South Africa, and Russia due to improved yields and acreage. Major exports are forecast slightly higher (+0.5 Mt) at 207.3 Mt.

In contrast, soybean stocks declined from 125.3 Mt to 124.8 Mt, as stronger global crush demand, especially in Brazil, offset modest production gains, with exports steady at 187.2 Mt.

Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape papers saw a volatile and active session, with the curve pushing higher across the board. Apr traded from a low of 27400 and was hit up to 28400, while May moved up sharply from 29400 to 31000. Jun also pushed higher from 30500 to 31500, with Q2 trading 28750 to 30250, Q3 went from 28000 to 29200, while Q4 moved up from 28500 to 29050. On the back end, Cal 27 traded between 25000 and 25300, with Cal 28 printing around 22900. Overall, it was a strong day for the market, with gains seen across the entire curve.

PMX
PMX papers saw a quiet session to end the week, with the curve trading relatively flat throughout the day. Apr traded only a few times between 17200 and 17100, while May moved between 18800 and 19100. Jun bounced around 19000 to 19250, with Q2 trading 18500 to 18400, Q3 traded from 18600 to 18350, while Q4 moved between 17000 and 16900. Cal 27 traded around 14650. Overall, it was a subdued end to the week, with the market holding steady across the curve.

SMX + HANDY
The SMX curve held steady, ticking up to start and trading within a narrow range over the day. Apr was paid up to 15500 during the morning session, now BOM 16218, but traded back to 15250 later in the day. Mar traded between 16400 – 17000, Jun 16700 – 16900 and Q2 16250 – 16500. Jul traded at 16600, while Q3 traded 16300 – 16500, Q4 between 15300 – 15350 and the C27 12900 – 13050. Handy Q3 traded 14150 – 14200 and the Cal27 traded 12350.

Carbon
EU carbon futures closed the week with a 1.2% decline amid very light trading activity. The Dec26 EUA Futures contract was assessed at €72.83, down €0.87, while traded volumes were less than 30m EUAs. Market activity is expected to increase next week as more traders return to their desks following Easter holidays.

Market Fundamentals
April WASDE: Wheat and Corn Stocks Raised, Soybeans
Tighten on Demand
Global wheat supply for 2025/26 increased from 277.0 Mt in
March to 283.1 Mt in the April WASDE, driven by higher
production in the EU and Russia alongside reduced
consumption, particularly in India. Global wheat exports
were marginally lowered by 0.3 Mt to 221.9 Mt.
Corn stocks also edged higher, rising from 292.7 Mt to 294.8
Mt (+2.1 Mt), supported by increased output in India, South
Africa, and Russia due to improved yields and acreage. Major
exports are forecast slightly higher (+0.5 Mt) at 207.3 Mt.
In contrast, soybean stocks declined from 125.3 Mt to 124.8
Mt, as stronger global crush demand, especially in Brazil,
oﬀset modest production gains, with exports steady at 187.2
Mt.
Trading Commentary
Cape
Cape papers saw a volatile and active session, with the curve
pushing higher across the board. Apr traded from a low of
27400 and was hit up to 28400, while May moved up sharply
from 29400 to 31000. Jun also pushed higher from 30500 to
31500, with Q2 trading 28750 to 30250, Q3 went from 28000
to 29200, while Q4 moved up from 28500 to 29050. On the
back end, Cal 27 traded between 25000 and 25300, with Cal
28 printing around 22900. Overall, it was a strong day for the
market, with gains seen across the entire curve.
PMX
PMX papers saw a quiet session to end the week, with the
curve trading relatively ﬂat throughout the day. Apr traded
only a few times between 17200 and 17100, while May
moved between 18800 and 19100. Jun bounced around
19000 to 19250, with Q2 trading 18500 to 18400, Q3 traded
from 18600 to 18350, while Q4 moved between 17000 and
16900. Cal 27 traded around 14650. Overall, it was a subdued
end to the week, with the market holding steady across the
curve.

The SMX curve held steady, ticking up to start and trading
within a narrow range over the day. Apr was paid up to
15500 during the morning session, now BOM 16218, but
traded back to 15250 later in the day. Mar traded between
16400 – 17000, Jun 16700 – 16900 and Q2 16250 – 16500. Jul
traded at 16600, while Q3 traded 16300 – 16500, Q4 between
15300 – 15350 and the C27 12900 – 13050. Handy Q3 traded

Handysize/Supramax Report10th April 2026
63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER      Paciﬁc: FIRMER           38,000 Atlantic: FLAT      Paciﬁc: FLAT
Atlantic Comment
The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) reached 2,095 points this week, marking a cautious
recovery as the market began pricing in a fragile two-week ceaseﬁre in the Middle
East. While the news of the Strait of Hormuz potentially reopening via alternative
routes oﬀered some psychological relief, bunker volatility remains extreme. This
spike in costs has kept voyage rates artiﬁcially high, particularly for Capesize vessels
in the Paciﬁc, even as actual demand from Chinese steel mills remains soft.
Meanwhile, the South Atlantic continues to carry the market's heavy lifting, with
Brazil’s soybean harvest now over 80% complete and a record 178-million-tonne crop
ﬂooding export terminals, ensuring a steady stream of cargo that is keeping vessel
supply tight despite the high cost of fuel.
On the Continent, the market has remained muted, with minimal cargo enquiry
continuing the trend seen last week. On the Handysize market, owners are rating
Trans-Atlantic trips on large Handys at around USD 17,000, though we have yet to
see these levels translate into ﬁxtures. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, we
saw a 61,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Antwerp for a trip to Turkey with steels at
USD 17,000, in line with levels seen last week, indicating a largely ﬂat market.
In the Mediterranean, the Handysize market saw very little activity, with sentiment
remaining largely positional, highlighted by the lack of reported ﬁxtures. Indicatively,
we saw a 35,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis Saﬁ for a short trip to South Spain at
USD 8,500. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, Trans-Atlantic trips are
continuing to ﬁx at around USD 10,000. We saw a 60,000 deadweight vessel ﬁx basis
Yesilovacik for a trip to redeliver in Brownsville at USD 10,000 for 50 days, although
the split for the balance is unknown.
The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has shown renewed strength
this week, with the supply-demand balance tipping back in favor of owners. This
ﬁrming sentiment was clearly highlighted by a recent ﬁxture where a large eco
Handysize secured $20,000 for a trip from Recalada to the West Mediterranean.
While other Atlantic regions have seen more modest movements, the ECSA basin
continues to lead the way, with owners successfully leveraging the steady ﬂow of
fresh inquiries to push rates back toward the psychological $20,000 threshold.
Despite a ﬂurry of activity for Supramax and Ultramax ECSA routes this week, the
market has essentially moved sideways as the industry navigates a condensed
trading window. The short work week between the Christian Easter and the
upcoming Orthodox Easter have created a sense of urgency among charterers to
cover prompt requirements, yet this uptick in inquiries has failed to translate into
signiﬁcant rate gains.
On the USG Handysize market, the week began on a quiet note due to the Monday
holiday across most markets, with sentiment initially weighed down by softer rate
levels carried over from last week. As activity resumed, we saw a bit more activity and
rates showing some slight improvement, with sentiment picking up a touch as the
week progressed. Owners are showing a bit more conﬁdence looking ahead to next
week, expecting the market to ﬁrm further. However, underlying fundamentals
remain somewhat unbalanced, with the tonnage list still longer than the available
cargo volume, limiting stronger upward momentum. The Supramax and Ultramax
market has continued to improve throughout the week, with Trans-Atlantic trips on
Ultramaxes now ﬁxing in the USD 20,000s. The remaining tonnage count for the
month appears well balanced against the inﬂux of fresh cargo enquiries seen over
the course of the week. For front-haul petcoke business, owners are now holding
levels closer to USD 25,000, representing a signiﬁcant increase of around USD 6,000
compared to last week, where similar ﬁxtures were concluded closer to USD 19,000.

Handysize/Supramax Report10th April 2026
Paciﬁc Comments
This week the Paciﬁc Supramax market remained ﬁrm overall, with macro developments continuing to inﬂuence sentiment.
The brief reopening of the Strait of Hormuz led to a temporary easing in bunker prices and a rise in FFA levels; however, the
subsequent closure quickly reintroduced uncertainty to both trade ﬂows and cost expectations. Against this backdrop, the
market was characterised by a strong period segment, ﬁrm spot support, and increasingly bullish owner sentiment.
The Indonesian coal sector showed signs of recovery, with an uptick in fresh cargoes and a noticeable drawdown of prompt
tonnage, leading to some improvement in regional balance. On the Indo/Seasia route, heard one UMX open Phils ﬁxed USD
19k for Indo/Phils; on Indo/China, levels also ﬁrmed, with heard one UMX open Singapore ﬁxed USD 17k and another SMX
open KSC ﬁxed USD 12.5k. The Indo/India (WCI) market remained well supported in terms of levels, although reported
ﬁxtures were limited, including heard one UMX del Cai Mei ﬁxed USD 19k, suggesting owners are still testing higher.
The North Vietnam / South China region continued to act as a key driver of the basin. Clinker exports from Vietnam to Bdesh
remained strong, with heard one SMX open S.China ﬁxed USD 20k. Additional ﬂows to West Africa were also noted, including
heard one UMX open Chaozhou ﬁxed USD 16,500 with split days. Bulk cement shipments to the USG were likewise active,
with heard one UMX open Cambodia ﬁxed USD 15.5k split. Meanwhile, the start of the nickel ore season has supported
activity, with heard one SMX open Xiamen ﬁxed USD 16k for nickel ore to North China.
The NOPAC market remained relatively stable, though activity was limited. Owners are currently oﬀering around USD 18k for
a NOPAC round, while charterers’ bids remain closer to USD 16k, leaving a noticeable gap and resulting in limited deal ﬂow.
In North China, steel and general cargo exports softened slightly in terms of activity, with fewer ﬁxtures reported. Bulk
cargoes, however, continued to provide support, including heard one SMX open N.China ﬁxed USD 18k for a trip to Sri Lanka
and another UMX ﬁxed at similar levels for BOP. The slag to Bdesh trade remained particularly ﬁrm, with UMX still achieving
USD 20k+.
The Australia market also maintained a ﬁrm tone, with steady cargo ﬂows across grains, salt, coal and ore. Heard one UMX
open Gresik ﬁxed USD 19k for Aus/Phils grains, and another UMX open ECI ﬁxed USD 14k dop for Aus/China grains, reﬂecting
continued support in the basin.
The period market remained strong, underpinned by both ﬁrm spot sentiment and FFA support. UMX short period ﬁxtures
were commonly concluded around USD 19k, while one-year deals held at approximately USD 17k–17.5k+, indicating
sustained owner conﬁdence in the near-term outlook.
Overall, the Paciﬁc Supramax market maintained a ﬁrm and slightly strengthening tone this week. With continued cargo ﬂow
and strong owner resistance, the market is likely to remain well supported in the short term, with potential for further upside
—let’s see next week!

STEADY IMPROVEMENT THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. FIXTURES REPORTED AT THE START OF THE WEEK WERE HEARD IN THE USD 23 /24K
RANGE. DEMAND STRENGTHENED AS THE WEEK PROGRESSED, WITH GRAIN HOUSES AND OPERATORS ACTIVELY ENTERING THE MARKET
TO SECURE COVERAGE. THIS SUSTAINED BUYING INTEREST, COMBINED WITH PROGRESSIVELY TIGHTER PROMPT TONNAGE AVAILABILITY,

Capesize Report10th April 2026
PAC: Busy         ATL: Firming
Market Comments
A more suppressed day in the Paciﬁc basin this morning despite two
majors present in the market. Activity was slow to pick up until the
Dampier major looked to secure their C5 stem for 26-28 April in line
with yesterday’s ﬁxtures. A bid at $11.70 was seen against $12.10
oﬀered before ﬁxing at $11.95. One major out of Hedland ﬁxed their
C5 stem at $12.15 for 23 April and rumored to have taken a
Newcastlemax too . Demand continues to show its strength in the
basin with a healthy level of C5 stems for end of April. A lot of tonnage
was cleared after a ﬂurry of early/mid May C3 stems were ﬁxed
yesterday afternoon with many reported to be in the very low $30s.
Regardless of yesterdays strong volumes - one German operator ﬁxed
their 08/12 cargo early doors at $30.15 C3 while a trader also
concluded for 05 May onwards at the same level. Tonnage remains
long as demand is moderate. Activity blossomed in the North Atlantic
yesterday afternoon as three fronthaul stems were seen to ﬁx in quick
succession. A miner concluded the day, securing their stem out of
Seven Islands to Oita for 01-07 May at $35.60 which out of Rotterdam
ran to $53,500 for a 79 day duration or a $1.65 mil score and $58,000
when run back to c9 duration. Meanwhile, into next week a couple of
fronthaul stems remain, as well as a slightly prompter backhaul cargo
out of South Africa.

Capesize Report10th April 2026
Market Comments
With several countries on holiday, Monday was slower in the Paciﬁc with limited activity occurring except for the usual
Indonesian operator ﬁxing a couple stems to Mundra for 15–21 April at mid $9.00s. Into Tuesday, activity resumed out of
West Australia as two majors were accompanied by strong operator C5 interest. Early bids at mid/high $11.00s were not
enough to tempt the mid $12's oﬀers, resulting in concession on the bid and the Dampier major taking a handful of vessels
at $12.25 for 21–23 April. Building in volume, activity picked up mid-week with three majors present. Rates however fell
marginally, a reﬂection primarily of the sizable drop in oil price the previous evening. Oﬀers readily lined up at mid $12.00s.
That day, a Dampier and a Hedland major each took a few at $12.15 with the Dampier major covering 22–24 and 24–26 April
while the Hedland major ﬁxed one earlier at $12.00. On the peripheral, a vessel ﬁxed from 11 April onwards for a TCT via
Newcastle redelivery China at $22,000, whilst an operator concluded their Newcastle to Mailiao stem for 01/10 May at high
$16.00’s. Volumes remained healthy through Thursday, although the trajectory of rates continued. Again oﬀers optimistically
congregated at $12.50 against bids at $11.60. With a further removal of support from the bunker price, the Dampier major
ﬁxed a handful at $11.85 C5. Operators bid the same levels on the follow, eager to capitalise on the softer oﬀers. prompting
other operators to bid at similar levels. On he peripheral, the usual Teluk operator ﬁxed a stem to Dung Quat for 20–22 April
with the last bid seen around $7.00. Sentiment clearly positive in the East rolling into the ﬁnal day of the week.
With most of Europe relaxing on Monday, the South did not ﬁnd rythm until mid-week. With a solid cargo book and owner's
ambition still to remain within the $30's C3, Tuesday got oﬀ to a slow start. An Ubu to Gwangyang tender concluded for 08–
17 May at mid $30s C3, oﬀering initial glimpses this ambition could be achieved and even built upon. In addition, a
Newcastlemax ﬁxed at $30 C3 for 06–10 May. Bids were initially stand-oﬃsh on Wednesday, as charterers watched oil prices
fall. Building in activity eventually into the afternoon, where an operator's stem for 10/11 May dates ﬁxed at $30, whilst a C17
concluded for 21–30 April at $21.85. A less frequent and forward Uruguay stem similarly concluded at $32.75. Counter
balancing the softer bunkers was a steady inﬂow of end April and early May cargoes, which eventually culminated in a robust
cargo book. Thursday saw the height of activity and where the basin created it's ﬂoor. Owners moved oﬀ their initial $31 C3
ideas as two Newcastlemaxes ﬁxed at $29.50 and high $29s C3, setting the tone. An array of rates from $30 to $30.50 C3
were then ﬁxed for 01-10 May dates on both capes and larger tonnage. This window now felt thinner on the tonnage, aided
by a further few stems being marketed that night. Come Friday, two standard capes were ﬁxed for early May at $30.15.
Fronthaul business, albeit the bulk of which forward, steadily rebalanced fundamentals in the North through the ﬁrst half of
the week. Tonnage however similarly light on the front end, as several vessel set their sights on West African business away
from the lackluster North last week. Continuing said trend, an end user ﬁxed a North continent ship for their Buchanan lift at
$28.85 for split dates. Out of Gibraltar, this ran to $57,000 for the duration and a score of $1.5m. Adjusted to C9 it was
equivalent to a healthy $56,300. With plenty of attractive fronthaul business available by Thursday, volumes spiked. First, an
interesting $57,500 for 76 days duration on a Newcastlemax with some additional legs at a lower rate. The second a double
discharge cargo to Taiwan that ﬁxed at $34.50. Adjusted to C9 ran to $56,300 or a $1.52 m score. Finally, late that evening a
miner concluded their Seven Islands to Oita for 01-07 May at $35.60 which out of Rotterdam ran to $58,000 C9 adjusted or
score of $1.65 mil score. Left for Friday was a few pieces of backhaul business and a smaller fronthaul stem, against only four
marketed vessels open for the remainder of April. Undoubtedly an interesting backdrop for the North to open with next
week.

items.parsed_text: Handysize/Supramax Report10th April 2026 63,500 Atlantic: FIRMER Pacific: FIRMER 38,000 Atlantic: FLAT Pacific: FLAT Atlantic Comment The Baltic Dry Index (BDI) reached 2,095 points this week, marking a cautious recovery as the market began pricing in a fragile two-week ceasefire in the Middle East. While the news of the Strait of Hormuz potentially reopening via alternative routes offered some psychological relief, bunker volatility remains extreme. This spike in costs has kept voyage rates artificially high, particularly for Capesize vessels in the Pacific, even as actual demand from Chinese steel mills remains soft. Meanwhile, the South Atlantic continues to carry the market's heavy lifting, with Brazil’s soybean harvest now over 80% complete and a record 178-million-tonne crop flooding export terminals, ensuring a steady stream of cargo that is keeping vessel supply tight despite the high cost of fuel. On the Continent, the market has remained muted, with minimal cargo enquiry continuing the trend seen last week. On the Handysize market, owners are rating Trans-Atlantic trips on large Handys at around USD 17,000, though we have yet to see these levels translate into fixtures. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, we saw a 61,000 deadweight vessel fix basis Antwerp for a trip to Turkey with steels at USD 17,000, in line with levels seen last week, indicating a largely flat market. In the Mediterranean, the Handysize market saw very little activity, with sentiment remaining largely positional, highlighted by the lack of reported fixtures. Indicatively, we saw a 35,000 deadweight vessel fix basis Safi for a short trip to South Spain at USD 8,500. On the Supramax and Ultramax market, Trans-Atlantic trips are continuing to fix at around USD 10,000. We saw a 60,000 deadweight vessel fix basis Yesilovacik for a trip to redeliver in Brownsville at USD 10,000 for 50 days, although the split for the balance is unknown. The East Coast South America (ECSA) Handysize market has shown renewed strength this week, with the supply-demand balance tipping back in favor of owners. This firming sentiment was clearly highlighted by a recent fixture where a large eco Handysize secured $20,000 for a trip from Recalada to the West Mediterranean. While other Atlantic regions have seen more modest movements, the ECSA basin continues to lead the way, with owners successfully leveraging the steady flow of fresh inquiries to push rates back toward the psychological $20,000 threshold. Despite a flurry of activity for Supramax and Ultramax ECSA routes this week, the market has essentially moved sideways as the industry navigates a condensed trading window. The short work week between the Christian Easter and the upcoming Orthodox Easter have created a sense of urgency among charterers to cover prompt requirements, yet this uptick in inquiries has failed to translate into significant rate gains. On the USG Handysize market, the week began on a quiet note due to the Monday holiday across most markets, with sentiment initially weighed down by softer rate levels carried over from last week. As activity resumed, we saw a bit more activity and rates showing some slight improvement, with sentiment picking up a touch as the week progressed. Owners are showing a bit more confidence looking ahead to next week, expecting the market to firm further. However, underlying fundamentals remain somewhat unbalanced, with the tonnage list still longer than the available cargo volume, limiting stronger upward momentum. The Supramax and Ultramax market has continued to improve throughout the week, with Trans-Atlantic trips on Ultramaxes now fixing in the USD 20,000s. The remaining tonnage count for the month appears well balanced against the influx of fresh cargo enquiries seen over the course of the week. For front-haul petcoke business, owners are now holding levels closer to USD 25,000, representing a significant increase of around USD 6,000 compared to last week, where similar fixtures were concluded closer to USD 19,000. The brief reopening of the Strait of Hormuz led to a temporary easing in bunker prices and a rise in FFA levels; however, the subsequent closure quickly reintroduced uncertainty to both trade flows and cost expectations. Against this backdrop, the market was characterised by a strong period segment, firm spot support, and increasingly bullish owner sentiment. The Indonesian coal sector showed signs of recovery, with an uptick in fresh cargoes and a noticeable drawdown of prompt tonnage, leading to some improvement in regional balance. On the Indo/Seasia route, heard one UMX open Phils fixed USD 19k for Indo/Phils; on Indo/China, levels also firmed, with heard one UMX open Singapore fixed USD 17k and another SMX open KSC fixed USD 12.5k. The Indo/India (WCI) market remained well supported in terms of levels, although reported fixtures were limited, including heard one UMX del Cai Mei fixed USD 19k, suggesting owners are still testing higher. The North Vietnam / South China region continued to act as a key driver of the basin. Clinker exports from Vietnam to Bdesh remained strong, with heard one SMX open S.China fixed USD 20k. Additional flows to West Africa were also noted, including heard one UMX open Chaozhou fixed USD 16,500 with split days. Bulk cement shipments to the USG were likewise active, with heard one UMX open Cambodia fixed USD 15.5k split. Meanwhile, the start of the nickel ore season has supported activity, with heard one SMX open Xiamen fixed USD 16k for nickel ore to North China. The NOPAC market remained relatively stable, though activity was limited. Owners are currently offering around USD 18k for a NOPAC round, while charterers’ bids remain closer to USD 16k, leaving a noticeable gap and resulting in limited deal flow. In North China, steel and general cargo exports softened slightly in terms of activity, with fewer fixtures reported. Bulk cargoes, however, continued to provide support, including heard one SMX open N.China fixed USD 18k for a trip to Sri Lanka and another UMX fixed at similar levels for BOP. The slag to Bdesh trade remained particularly firm, with UMX still achieving USD 20k+. The Australia market also maintained a firm tone, with steady cargo flows across grains, salt, coal and ore. Heard one UMX open Gresik fixed USD 19k for Aus/Phils grains, and another UMX open ECI fixed USD 14k dop for Aus/China grains, reflecting continued support in the basin. The period market remained strong, underpinned by both firm spot sentiment and FFA support. UMX short period fixtures were commonly concluded around USD 19k, while one-year deals held at approximately USD 17k–17.5k+, indicating sustained owner confidence in the near-term outlook. Overall, the Pacific Supramax market maintained a firm and slightly strengthening tone this week. With continued cargo flow and strong owner resistance, the market is likely to remain well supported in the short term, with potential for further upside —let’s see next week! items.parsed_text: Panam ax/Kamsarmax Report10th April 2026 ATL: FIRMER PAC: FIRMER MID EAST: FIRMER Market Comments ATL SHORT: MARKET OUTLOOK - SUBJECT TO NO UNEXPECTED GEOPOLITICAL DEVELOPMENTS IN THE MIDDLE EAST OVER THE WEEKEND, THE OUTLOOK FOR FRONT HAUL ACTIVITY REMAINS SUPPORTIVE. IF WE SEE STRENGTHENING GRAIN DEMAND EX ECSA AND SUSTAINED ACTIVITY FROM NCSA, IT SHOULD PROVIDE SUFFICIENT SUPPORT FOR OWNERS TO MAINTAIN OR INCREASE CURRENT OFFER LEVELS PAC SHORT: THIS WEEK WAS A SLOW BURN WITH MOST OF THE SHIPPING WORLD STILL OFF FOR MONDAY DUE TO VARIOUS HOLIDAYS. DEMAND OPENEND SOLID FOR BOTH NOPAC AND INDO WHICH REMAINED A CONSISTENT THEME THROUGHOUT THE WEEK. THE HESITANT FLOOR FOUND AT THE END OF LAST WEEK CONTINUED WITH NOPAC SPREADS STARTING THE WEEK AROUND LOW 15’S VS LOW 16’S BKI CJK. TONNAGE SUPPLY IS RELATIVELY TIGHT WITH RESPECT TO THE INCREASED DEMAND WITH 10+ NOPAC GRAINS CARGOES IN THE MARKET. BY WEEK END WE SAW FIXTURES WELL INTO THE 17’S BKI CJK FOR EARLY MAY LOADERS. FOR E.AUS WE HAVE STARTED TO SEE A BIT OF LIFE SINCE THE UNREST IN THE MIDDLE EAST. A SOLID AMOUNT OF E.AUS DEMAND MAINLY FOCUSSED ON REPOZ AND BHP CARGOES WITH FORWARD SHIPS FIXING AT HIGHS OF MID 17’S BKI FOR EARLY MAY LOADERS BY WEDNESDAY. THE POINT OF CONTENTION HAS BEEN AROUND FWD MAY CARGOES WITH INCREASED APPETITE, SO THE LARGER OPERATORS WERE LOOKING TO TAKE COVER 1K+ ABOVE CURRENT MARKET FIXTURES. BY FRIDAY EAUS ROUNDS WERE FIXING INTO THE MID 17’S BKI CJK, A SOLID 1K-1.5K JUMP COMPARED TO THIS TIME LAST WEEK. INDO OPENED THE WEEK AS THE FRONT RUNNER WITH FIXTURES JUMPING TO 16K BKI HK BY TUESDAY. CARGO COUNT REMAINED FIRM THROUGHOUT THE WEEK WITH CHINESE OPERATORS STARTING TO TAKE COVER AGAIN BSS NO SUBS. MIDWEEK SAW A SOLID INFLUX OF OF BOTH JAPANESE TENDERS AND SEASIA (BOR AOB/MAX 15 YEARS) CARGOES WHICH DROVE THE PREMIUM FOR MORE ECO UNITS. OVERALL, BASIN FUNDAMENTALS SEEM TO REMAIN IN OWNERS' FAVOUR WITH A HEALTHY P6 AND FORWARD CURVE TO SUPPORT, AND WE EXPECT THE MARKET TO CONTINUE ON A SIMILAR STEADY CLIMB UPWARDS. THIS SUSTAINED BUYING INTEREST, COMBINED WITH PROGRESSIVELY TIGHTER PROMPT TONNAGE AVAILABILITY, RESULTED IN A GRADUAL STRENGTHENING OF RATES. BY THE END OF THE WEEK, FIXTURES WERE REPORTED CLOSING IN THE USD 25 / 26K RANGE, MARKING A CLEAR IMPROVEMENT FROM EARLY WEEK LEVELS. items.parsed_text: Capesize Report10th April 2026 PAC: Busy ATL: Firming Market Comments A more suppressed day in the Pacific basin this morning despite two majors present in the market. Activity was slow to pick up until the Dampier major looked to secure their C5 stem for 26-28 April in line with yesterday’s fixtures. A bid at $11.70 was seen against $12.10 offered before fixing at $11.95. One major out of Hedland fixed their C5 stem at $12.15 for 23 April and rumored to have taken a Newcastlemax too . Demand continues to show its strength in the basin with a healthy level of C5 stems for end of April. A lot of tonnage was cleared after a flurry of early/mid May C3 stems were fixed yesterday afternoon with many reported to be in the very low $30s. Regardless of yesterdays strong volumes - one German operator fixed their 08/12 cargo early doors at $30.15 C3 while a trader also concluded for 05 May onwards at the same level. Tonnage remains long as demand is moderate. Activity blossomed in the North Atlantic yesterday afternoon as three fronthaul stems were seen to fix in quick succession. A miner concluded the day, securing their stem out of Seven Islands to Oita for 01-07 May at $35.60 which out of Rotterdam ran to $53,500 for a 79 day duration or a $1.65 mil score and $58,000 when run back to c9 duration. Meanwhile, into next week a couple of fronthaul stems remain, as well as a slightly prompter backhaul cargo out of South Africa. Into Tuesday, activity resumed out of West Australia as two majors were accompanied by strong operator C5 interest. Early bids at mid/high $11.00s were not enough to tempt the mid $12's offers, resulting in concession on the bid and the Dampier major taking a handful of vessels at $12.25 for 21–23 April. Building in volume, activity picked up mid-week with three majors present. Rates however fell marginally, a reflection primarily of the sizable drop in oil price the previous evening. Offers readily lined up at mid $12.00s. That day, a Dampier and a Hedland major each took a few at $12.15 with the Dampier major covering 22–24 and 24–26 April while the Hedland major fixed one earlier at $12.00. On the peripheral, a vessel fixed from 11 April onwards for a TCT via Newcastle redelivery China at $22,000, whilst an operator concluded their Newcastle to Mailiao stem for 01/10 May at high $16.00’s. Volumes remained healthy through Thursday, although the trajectory of rates continued. Again offers optimistically congregated at $12.50 against bids at $11.60. With a further removal of support from the bunker price, the Dampier major fixed a handful at $11.85 C5. Operators bid the same levels on the follow, eager to capitalise on the softer offers. prompting other operators to bid at similar levels. On he peripheral, the usual Teluk operator fixed a stem to Dung Quat for 20–22 April with the last bid seen around $7.00. Sentiment clearly positive in the East rolling into the final day of the week. With most of Europe relaxing on Monday, the South did not find rythm until mid-week. With a solid cargo book and owner's ambition still to remain within the $30's C3, Tuesday got off to a slow start. An Ubu to Gwangyang tender concluded for 08– 17 May at mid $30s C3, offering initial glimpses this ambition could be achieved and even built upon. In addition, a Newcastlemax fixed at $30 C3 for 06–10 May. Bids were initially stand-oﬃsh on Wednesday, as charterers watched oil prices fall. Building in activity eventually into the afternoon, where an operator's stem for 10/11 May dates fixed at $30, whilst a C17 concluded for 21–30 April at $21.85. A less frequent and forward Uruguay stem similarly concluded at $32.75. Counter balancing the softer bunkers was a steady inflow of end April and early May cargoes, which eventually culminated in a robust cargo book. Thursday saw the height of activity and where the basin created it's floor. Owners moved off their initial $31 C3 ideas as two Newcastlemaxes fixed at $29.50 and high $29s C3, setting the tone. An array of rates from $30 to $30.50 C3 were then fixed for 01-10 May dates on both capes and larger tonnage. This window now felt thinner on the tonnage, aided by a further few stems being marketed that night. Come Friday, two standard capes were fixed for early May at $30.15. Fronthaul business, albeit the bulk of which forward, steadily rebalanced fundamentals in the North through the first half of the week. Tonnage however similarly light on the front end, as several vessel set their sights on West African business away from the lackluster North last week. Continuing said trend, an end user fixed a North continent ship for their Buchanan lift at $28.85 for split dates. Out of Gibraltar, this ran to $57,000 for the duration and a score of $1.5m. Adjusted to C9 it was equivalent to a healthy $56,300. With plenty of attractive fronthaul business available by Thursday, volumes spiked. First, an interesting $57,500 for 76 days duration on a Newcastlemax with some additional legs at a lower rate. The second a double discharge cargo to Taiwan that fixed at $34.50. Adjusted to C9 ran to $56,300 or a $1.52 m score. Finally, late that evening a miner concluded their Seven Islands to Oita for 01-07 May at $35.60 which out of Rotterdam ran to $58,000 C9 adjusted or score of $1.65 mil score. Left for Friday was a few pieces of backhaul business and a smaller fronthaul stem, against only four marketed vessels open for the remainder of April. Undoubtedly an interesting backdrop for the North to open with next week. Global wheat exports were marginally lowered by 0.3 Mt to 221.9 Mt. Corn stocks also edged higher, rising from 292.7 Mt to 294.8 Mt (+2.1 Mt), supported by increased output in India, South Africa, and Russia due to improved yields and acreage. Major exports are forecast slightly higher (+0.5 Mt) at 207.3 Mt. In contrast, soybean stocks declined from 125.3 Mt to 124.8 Mt, as stronger global crush demand, especially in Brazil, offset modest production gains, with exports steady at 187.2 Mt. Trading Commentary Cape Cape papers saw a volatile and active session, with the curve pushing higher across the board. Apr traded from a low of 27400 and was hit up to 28400, while May moved up sharply from 29400 to 31000. Jun also pushed higher from 30500 to 31500, with Q2 trading 28750 to 30250, Q3 went from 28000 to 29200, while Q4 moved up from 28500 to 29050. On the back end, Cal 27 traded between 25000 and 25300, with Cal 28 printing around 22900. Overall, it was a strong day for the market, with gains seen across the entire curve. PMX PMX papers saw a quiet session to end the week, with the curve trading relatively flat throughout the day. Apr traded only a few times between 17200 and 17100, while May moved between 18800 and 19100. Jun bounced around 19000 to 19250, with Q2 trading 18500 to 18400, Q3 traded from 18600 to 18350, while Q4 moved between 17000 and 16900. Cal 27 traded around 14650. Overall, it was a subdued end to the week, with the market holding steady across the curve. SMX + HANDY The SMX curve held steady, ticking up to start and trading within a narrow range over the day. Apr was paid up to 15500 during the morning session, now BOM 16218, but traded back to 15250 later in the day. Mar traded between 16400 – 17000, Jun 16700 – 16900 and Q2 16250 – 16500. Jul traded at 16600, while Q3 traded 16300 – 16500, Q4 between 15300 – 15350 and the C27 12900 – 13050.
